title: CLAY COUNTY BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay County Board met Tuesday night in the upstairs courtroom of the courthouse in Louisville.

Chairman Joe Goodman called the meeting to order and members quickly approved the meeting agenda and past meeting minutes. Claims Committee member Terry Hronec went over the Claims Committee Report. It shows Paid Claims totaling $4,388,856 and Unpaid Claims of $42,851. The board approved the report unanimously.

Jennifer Brown submitted the 911 Report for July. During her report, it was announced that Curtis Leib ended his time on the 911 Board after six years of service, with thanks from fellow members. Brown presented the name of Tom Allen as Leib’s replacement for a three-year term ending in August of 2029, and the board approved it without dissent.

Clay County Hospital President/CEO Bob Sellers presented the Hospital Report. He began by asking for board approval of the CCH audit by Blue and Company, which revealed no discrepancies. Sellers mentioned a few strong key financial figures which show excellent results for the hospital. Sellers offered credit to Jennifer Venable and other members of the team. The board approved acceptance of the audit. He then shifted to correct information about the construction on the hospital campus. He noted that the contractor expected to move around 350 truckloads of dirt. He said the figure is now up to 700, and some people have expressed concern that it would raise the project costs. But Sellers noted that the issue is between the contractor and the vendor and won’t affect the cost. The CCH leader said that President Trump is offering the $50 Billion Rural Health Transformation Program as part of a five-year federal initiative established by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act to strengthen rural healthcare. Some $10 Billion will be allocated annually from 2026-2030. Sellers adds Clay County Hospital wants to make sure it receives its allotment; they expect it to be in the neighborhood of $265,000 but were told it would be more like $350,000 for planning purposes. Next, Sellers presented three Capital Expense items for purchase. The MindRay Vital Sign Monitors will improve the safety of patients as the 25 devices will automatically record patient vitals into their electronic records, eliminating errors. The cost was put at $272,834 and the board approved it. The board also approved two other items unanimously, namely USAC Network Equipment for $86,259 and new construction Network Equipment for $63,761. The items are for the hospital addition and the Clay County Health Department construction. The board also approved medical staff credentials for healthcare professionals.

Clay County Health Department Administrator Jeff Workman presented the Board of Health Report. He cited various items from the report including roof storm damage at Beyond the Bell as well as concern about their parking lot. Workman briefly addressed the Lone Star Tick concern in Illinois. Those bites cause Alpha-gal syndrome, which results in victims becoming allergic to red meat. The state is doing tick surveillance to monitor the problem as Illinois is considered an area of concern and doctors are encouraged to consider Alpha-gal syndrome in patients that present with symptoms. Workman also noted the Cyclospora outbreak that has expanded from infected lettuce to now include jalapeños. Workman also mentioned the S.U.R.E. Symposium that took place earlier in the day at Oil Belt Christian Service Camp and he had heard good things about the event. He also reminded parents to get student immunizations before school starts with the health dept. offering clinics on Thursday and Friday if needed. The health dept also offers Cologuard for colon cancer screenings. Workman also noted they are seeking an RN for their Home Care program. He closed out his report noting that their Hospice program has once again earned honors for excellence in delivering exceptional care.

Jeremy Bookland with Magoo and Associates updated the board on IT issues for the county. He noted that 698 tickets for service had been submitted and only seven remain open. They are looking at updating equipment in the courthouse that will result in improved network reliability and performance and reduce the risk of hardware failure. They encourage all departments to migrate to .gov email addresses as a means to deal with the increase in malicious and phishing emails. They are also encouraging their customers to use password management to better safeguard online accounts. They’re also looking for workstations to have battery backups available and encourage departments to use lockable enclosed server racks for IT equipment.

The board approved the 2027 Holiday Schedule as presented and then County Clerk Amy Britton presented the Clay County Board meeting schedule for 2027. Meetings will continue to be on the second Tuesday of each month, with the exception of April, when all Illinois Townships meet on the second Tuesday, meaning the county board meeting will be on April 15 at 6:00pm. The board approved the schedule.

In the Chairman’s Report, Joe Goodman noted comments he has received concerning the financing of the 708 board that deals with Mental Health issues, saying they will look at it in the months ahead as it is included in the tax levy. Goodman also noted that Animal Control has lost employee Katie Klanke and the position is listed as open.

The meeting then went into executive or closed session. When they returned to the open meeting Goodman announced the closed session was informational only. And with all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: TRUCKER ATTACKED
full_story:
A Rockford truck driver is recovering from serious injuries after he was the victim of a violent attack while making a stop in Effingham Saturday morning.

Meiborg Companies, a trucking company based in Rockford, shared a Facebook post Monday identifying the driver as Corey Clayton and asking the community to support him during his recovery.  According to the company, Clayton had stopped for the night to rest at the Travel Centers of America, before completing the final leg of his trip home when he was allegedly attacked by multiple individuals.  According to the company Clayton was beaten so severely that he lost consciousness.  Another truck driver reportedly came upon the scene and chased the attackers away before emergency responders arrived.  Clayton was then airlifted to Carle Foundation Hospital in Urbana for treatment.

Information gathered through the initial investigation indicates this was an isolated incident, and Effingham Police say there is no known ongoing threat to the community.  The Effingham Police Department is asking anyone with information that may assist investigators to contact them.

title: XENIA VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
Last night’s Xenia Village Board meeting began with public comments from Engineer Brandon Bridges with Charleston Engineering.  Bridges shared updated information with Xenia Village Board of trustees following last months decision to preform a title search to determine the ownership of a stretch of road along Main Street to the railroad tracks.  Bridges told trustees that through court records he was able to determine that stretch of road belongs to CSX railroad.  This means that Trustees will need to request permission from CSX to repave 50 feet of road and require a flagger at the crossing extending the timeline for the villages $1,075,000 road resurfacing project.

Vince King then spoke with trustees and requested approval to use of the school/community building for parking for the August 22nd Xenia Fire department Fish Fry.

No new updates have been provided to trustees regarding the renovation and staffing of the village’s gas station.  Trustees also shared that village residents who had received ordnance violation notices were making efforts to bring their properties into compliance.

Village Superintendent Travis Lewis told trustees “water and sewer in the village was flowing well” following replacement of a starter at the villages south east lift station.  Lewis also shared that the previously discussed drainage ditch to address flooding along one road in the village has been dug.

Xenia Chief of Police Jerry Burkett reported to trustees that things were going well and that he was awaiting installation of mobile data center in department vehicles following updates.

Trustees then turned their attention to building maintenance and the option to construct a new community building.  Trustees voted to move forward with plans to construct a new building following the securing of loans and bids for construction of the building along with approval of construction plans.  There is no clear budget or timeline for the project at this time.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross announced an emergency blood shortage on July 13th.  Despite thousands of individuals stepping forward to help, the situation has escalated into a blood supply CRISIS.  For just the second time in history, the Red Cross has issued a national blood CRISIS.  Blood donations have fallen to a four-year summer low, worsening this summer’s emergency shortage.  A blood supply crisis is the most extreme blood shortage, posing a concerning risk to patient care.  Doctors will be forced to make difficult decisions about who receives blood transfusions and who will need to wait until more blood products become available.

The American Red Cross needs your help now so that hospital patients can continue to receive the transfusions they need.  All blood types are needed, but the situation is especially dire for type O blood as the Red Cross is now limiting distribution of these blood products to hospitals.  The type O positive blood supply has fallen below a one-day supply.  Blood donors are needed immediately to ensure hospitals have the blood they need for patients whose lives depend on transfusions.

To ease the shortage the American Red Cross has scheduled a Blood Drive for tomorrow at the Flora Church of the Nazarene from noon to 5 pm.  People donating at this drive will get a $20 Amazon Gift Card by email.

After tomorrows drive there will be a Blood Drive on Tuesday, August 18th from 2 to 6 pm at the Mason Christian Church, and then on Friday, August 31st at the Clay City High School from 1 to 5 pm sponsored by the Clay City High School Student Council.  By donating at this drive, donors are helping one or more graduating seniors earn a scholarship.

title: XENIA FIRE DEPARTMENT CALL
full_story:
On Monday at approximately 10:40 am, the Xenia Fire Protection District was dispatched to a report of a hay bale on fire next to several other hay bales in the 2500 block of Cypress Drive.

Upon arrival, firefighters found one hay bale actively burning.  Prior to the fire department’s arrival, the caller had moved the burning bale away from the surrounding hay bales, helping prevent the fire from spreading.

Firefighters, with assistance from a nearby neighbor and their tractor, broke the burning bale apart to expose the fire and extinguished it.

The Xenia Fire Protection District responded with seven firefighters and two engines.  Crews remained on scene for just over 30 minutes to extinguish the fire and ensure there was no further threat of rekindling.

title: CLAY COUNTY SHERIFF’S ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Clay County Sheriff Andy Myers issued his monthly activity report during Tuesday’s Clay County Board meeting.  In the Report for July, the Sheriff’s Office issued a total of 15 Traffic Citations, made 30 Criminal Arrests and served 26 various Civil Papers.  A total of 20,348 miles were driven by Sheriff’s personnel during the month.

30 persons were processed through the Clay County Jail during July.  There were 9 inmates in jail at the beginning of the month and 6 in jail at the end of the month.  The average daily jail population was 9.

Also, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office received a total of $1,186 during the month.  This includes:

The Sheriff’s Office handled approximately 566 complaints, 111 of which originated in Louisville and 86 in Clay City.  The Sheriff’s Office conducted 32 Criminal Investigations and 17 Accident Investigations during July.

title: PUBLIC INFORMATION MEETING
full_story:
The City of Flora will have a public information meeting on Monday, August 17th at 4:15 pm.  The city is pursuing funding through the Illinois Transportation Enhancement Program (ITEP) for proposed sidewalk improvements to create safer pedestrian routes to local schools and the industrial park.

Residents, parents, property owners, employees, and community members are encouraged to attend, learn about the proposed project, ask questions, and share input.

The city needs the community to show their support for the project.  The meeting will be at 4:15 pm on Monday, August 17th at Flora City Hall.

title: XENIA FIRE DEPARTMENT FISH FRY
full_story:
The Xenia Fire Department Fish Fry will be held on Saturday, August 22nd in the Xenia Village Park.  Lunch will be served starting at 11 am.  Along with fish sandwiches there will be hot dogs, fries and drinks.  There will also be vendors and a flavored lemonade stand.

The tractor pull and car show registration begin at Noon with admission $10 for adults and children 12 and under are free.  Pit passes are $15.  Car show awards will be at 3 pm.

There will be Carnival Games and prizes, inflatables and a petting zoo from Noon to 4 pm, with a $3 armband available good for unlimited activities.  There will be a silent auction at Noon.  The cake walk will be at 4 pm, bingo in the fire station starts at 5 pm and there will be live music from 7 to 10 pm.

All proceeds from the day go to the Xenia Volunteer Fire Department.

title: FRIENDS OF THE LIBRARY FALL BOOK SALE
full_story:
The Friends of the Flora Public Library Fall Book Sale will be held on Saturday, September 12th from 8 am to 3 pm.

Anyone wishing to contribute to the book sale can bring books that are in good shape to the front desk.  The Flora Public Library is open Monday through Thursday 1:00 – 8:00 pm, Friday 10:00 am to 6:00 pm and Saturday 10:00 am to 3:00 pm.  The library has a handcart to assist individuals who may be bringing a large volume of materials in.

The day of the sale all books, DVD’s and CD’s will be .25 cents.  Magazines are 10 cents each or 12 for $1.
